mechanism_narrative: The steady rise in WORKPLACES mobility from -3.4 to +2.0 over the four weeks ending 2022-09-15 signals a return to commuting routines; this lifts weekday retail footfall and pushes RETAIL_REC above its last 28-day mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its mean over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining positive.

mechanism_narrative: A joint pattern of TRANSIT holding above +6% while RESIDENTIAL falls from +8.6 to +5.1 indicates out-of-home substitution; this diversion of activity from home to transit corridors should raise RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not exceed its last 14-day mean when TRANSIT is above +6% and RESIDENTIAL is below +6%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM staying above +13% above baseline reflects precautionary stockpiling; when it crosses +15% as in t-1w, households cut discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC should fall over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean when GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean is above +15%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remaining near -13% below baseline in mid-September is consistent with seasonal heat/rain pushing activity indoors; this substitution should support indoor retail-and-recreation footfall and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last 28-day mean while PARKS remains below -10%.

mechanism_narrative: In a stable reopening-policy regime, positive TRANSIT and WORKPLACES above baseline indicate durable resumption of public activity; this policy-stability channel should keep RETAIL_REC improving over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays above +5% and WORKPLACES stays above 0% for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not higher than its last 28-day mean while TRANSIT > +5% and WORKPLACES > 0% persist.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility above +6% would signal renewed stay-at-home behavior from policy tightening or health caution; that would suppress discretionary retail trips and drive RETAIL_REC lower over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is higher than its last 7-day mean when RESIDENTIAL weekly mean is above +6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of GROCERY_PHARM above +14% and PARKS below -12% indicates a home-centered, low-outdoor-activity week; this behavioral configuration predicts reduced discretionary retail traffic and lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM > +14% and PARKS < -12% in the same week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean when GROCERY_PHARM > +14% and PARKS < -12% jointly occur.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES crossing from negative to positive territory for two weeks marks a regime shift toward office attendance; this shift should raise weekday retail demand and push RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean > 0% for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than its last 14-day mean after WORKPLACES stays above 0% for two consecutive weeks.
